body.x: IMPACTIVE AI (CEO Doohee Chung) participated in the “Global Media Online Meetup” on July 4, co-hosted by Ubergizmo and AVING News, introducing Korean startups to global audiences—the event aimed to promote CES 2026 Innovation Award candidates and expand media and business exposure.

Founded in 2021, IMPACTIVE AI is a demand forecasting solution provider that leverages AI to enhance corporate decision-making. Its R&D team, composed of Ph.D.-level experts from Seoul National University, Harvard, and KAIST, developed Deepflow—a next-generation forecasting platform integrating machine learning and deep learning.

Deepflow supports demand forecasting, raw material price and usage estimation, new product performance prediction, and consumer preference analysis. With customizable models and automated analysis pipelines, Deepflow delivers superior accuracy and deployment efficiency compared to competitors.

Since 2023, Deepflow has been adopted by major corporations in steel, pharmaceuticals, fragrance, food, manufacturing, and apparel. A steel company reduced stockouts by 37.8%, overstock by 25.5%, and saved approximately KRW 21 billion monthly. In pharma, Deepflow improved OTC forecasting accuracy from 50% to 81%, reducing stockouts and inventory losses.

body.cap: Deepflow Demand Forecast Visualization | Image courtesy of IMPACTIVE AI

body.x: In global markets, IMPACTIVE AI successfully implemented a PoC with a leading U.S. furniture brand, proving Deepflow’s scalability for international manufacturing and retail networks. Collaborations with Germany’s Fraunhofer IWU and a victory at the Driverly Berlin tech competition further solidified its credibility. The company holds 61 patents and has raised KRW 10.8 billion from investors, including CJ, Lotte, Hyundai, and IBK Venture Capital.

At CES 2026, IMPACTIVE AI introduces Quantum Deepflow, the world’s first quantum mechanics-based industrial time-series forecasting system. It utilizes quantum principles like superposition and entanglement to deliver accuracy and speed beyond traditional deep learning methods.

Quantum Deepflow combines a Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) architecture with deep learning to learn high-dimensional nonlinear patterns. Quantum circuits enhance prediction gates for maximum effect. A lightweight QLSTM architecture runs efficiently even in NISQ environments with shallow depth and low qubit requirements, compatible with both simulators and quantum hardware.

The system’s accuracy improved by 49% over conventional deep learning. A Korean steel company using the beta version achieved 98–99% accuracy in predicting 30-day futures prices for copper, nickel, gold, and aluminum. Simulations showed 35.4% fewer stockouts, 32.2% less overstock, and annual savings of $15 million.

body.cap: Korean Logo of Impactive AI | Image provided by Impactive AI

body.x: Quantum Deepflow enhances user experience through explainable AI visualizations, highlighting key variables and risk factors. Its UI flows from prediction to KPI simulation and procurement strategy, enabling purchasing managers to make optimal decisions directly within the platform.
The system features visual tools like QLSTM-based uncertainty intervals and side-by-side comparisons with traditional models, offering transparency, efficiency, and usability.

Quantum Deepflow introduces three innovations redefining industrial forecasting: 1) hybrid quantum deep learning architecture optimized for NISQ, 2) first application of quantum forecasting to real-world time-series data, and 3) patented end-to-end automation technologies—including hybrid prediction engines, denoising autoencoders, and KPI-based strategy recommendation pipelines.

According to the company, these breakthroughs mark a turning point in applying quantum AI from labs to factories. Quantum Deepflow minimizes power consumption compared to GPU-based systems, contributing to sustainability while optimizing purchase timing and inventory strategy.

An IMPACTIVE AI spokesperson stated, “Quantum Deepflow integrates into our SaaS platform Deepflow, enabling clients to predict real-time fluctuations and automate optimal procurement and inventory strategies. It reduces costs, inventory risks, and decision-making time.”

They added, “This is a leading example of deploying quantum-based forecasting in volatile procurement markets as a real-world online AI service. We will continue to drive both technological and commercial growth to lead in the global market.”

Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo operates the Silicon Valley Post and publishes content in six languages across 200 countries, with a focus on electronics and technology. It regularly covers major global exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo co-founder and CTO Hubert Nguyen attended the event. He previously worked as an NVIDIA programming engineer, developer education program manager, and 3D graphics programmer. He covers products and technologies from around the world at CES each year.
